title: CEN/CENELEC JTC 21 — EU AI Act Harmonised Standards Pipeline Q3 2026
context: 2026-08-30 engine cycle — CEN/CENELEC JTC 21 drafts harmonised standards giving presumption of conformity under the EU AI Act; first batch expected for Commission review Q4 2026, adoption mid-2027
body: CEN/CENELEC Joint Technical Committee 21 is the European standards body drafting harmonised standards that provide a presumption of conformity with the EU AI Act essential requirements. Operators following a harmonised standard do not need to prove compliance from first principles — the standard is the safe harbour. The JTC 21 work programme covers risk management systems aligned with ISO/IEC 23894, data quality and governance, transparency and information provision, human oversight mechanisms, and accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity for high-risk AI systems. The Commission issued its standardisation request in May 2023; first draft standards are expected for review in Q4 2026, with adoption targeted by mid-2027 — just as the high-risk obligations phase in. For a verification-first operator, harmonised standards are a floor, not a ceiling: a verified measurement credential wraps a compliance artifact in an independently signed envelope, making the presumption auditable rather than self-declared. The Council of AI treats JTC 21 as a boundary-instrumentation opportunity: every harmonised standard is a measurable axis. Monitored containment, not provable isolation: the standard does not guarantee safety, but a signed credential proves the operator was measured against it and the result is tamper-evident.
